text:
Priya: Heads-up — planning to roll out the new rate_limit policy (v3) to /v2/generate tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Canary start at 2% traffic, then 10% after 30m, then 50% after 2h if no regressions. Need SRE + support eyes for the canary window.
Liam: :eyes: thanks. Can you paste the exact config diff? want to validate header parsing and burst window math.
Priya: TL;DR: raising per-tenant RPS from 10->15, keeping token-based quotas, reducing short-burst allowance (burst_window: 2s -> 1s) to control concurrent inflight. Full diff:```json
{
  "policy_version": "v3",
  "global": { "default_rps": 15, "burst_window_seconds": 1, "max_burst_tokens": 300 },
  "overrides": [{ "path_prefix": "/v2/embeddings", "rps": 8 }]
}```
Zoe: That burst_window change is the risky bit — some clients rely on brief burst spikes (clients doing parallel chat calls). How will we detect false positives vs legit spikes?
Alex: We have scoped metrics: token_ingress_rate, request_concurrency, 429_by_reason. Recommend alert: 429_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m for the canary + increase in p95 latency by >150ms.
Carmen: Support: we'll have a banner and email template ready for affected customers. Also prepping repro steps if they hit 429s: collect client-ip, API-key-hash, request-timestamp, and a short request sample.
Priya: Good. Rollout plan: 1) push policy to canary fleet at 09:00, 2) run smoke for 10m (synthetic traffic + internal dev traffic), 3) open 30m observation window at 2%: SLI watch (420/429 streams), 4) if green, increase to 10%, wait 30m, then 50% after 2h.
Liam: Who holds the rollback key if we hit escalations? I can rollback the policy in infra but want product/SRE signoff.
Priya: Rollback owner = Liam (eng-sre) for infra flip. Carmen (support) owns customer comms. Zoe (eng-platform) holds go/no-go for config anomalies. Alex to own metrics checks and runbook triggers.
support-bot: Scheduled policy_push job queued: policy=v3, target=/v2/generate, canary_percent=2, eta=2026-04-03T09:00:00Z
Zoe: Added one more check: cache-hit-rate for prefix-cache. Reducing burst_window may increase cache misses early in sequences. Add metric: cache_hit_rate drop >5% triggers hold.
Alex: Noted. I'll add those thresholds to the canary dashboard. Also adding automated smoke to replay a set of 50 recorded customer sessions to detect auth/parsing regressions.
Priya: On rollback criteria — let's be explicit: immediate rollback if any of: 1) sustained 429_rate >1% for 5m, 2) p95 latency increase >250ms for 5m, 3) cache_hit_rate drops >10% and correlates with 5xx/429 spike, 4) any customer-reported auth failures >3 distinct API keys within 30m.
Carmen: Support playbook: when rollback occurs, we set incident severity to P2, open a dedicated thread, and start outreach for keys showing >5 429s. Template ready.
Liam: On the infra side, rollback will be `policyctl revert --target /v2/generate --to-version v2` and verify propagation. That usually takes ~40s to hit all canaries, full fleet ~6-8m. I'll run that if Alex flags metric thresholds or if Priya calls it.
Priya: Ok. Also note: there's a known parsing edge case in our header-checker for X-Client-Id with spaces. Patch merged yesterday, but only in canary runtime image. If we see auth header rejections, we'll need to flip runtime image to previous one, not just policy.
Zoe: Good catch. I'll watch header_rejects metric separately.
support-bot: Reminder: runbook link -> https://internal/redwood/runbooks/rate-limit-rollout
Alex: Quick question about observability: do we have token-level attribution for 429s? we need to map 429 -> API key hash quickly for outreach.
Priya: Yes, logs include api_key_hash and trace_id. We're also shipping a lightweight analytic event to the canary collector so you can query: `select count(*) from canary_events where reason='429' group by api_key_hash`
Carmen: For support triage, please ensure we capture request body snippets (first 1KB) and truncated headers. Privacy-preserving policy: redact user content and store snippet with retention 7d.
Liam: Ops note: coordinate with Network for any spikes in SYN errors — rate changes can cause unexpected client backoff patterns. I put a calendar block for 08:45–11:30 UTC to be reachable.
Priya: Deploy bot will post when push starts. During canary window, ping #eng-oncall and #support-escalations for live updates.
deploy-bot: policy_push started at 2026-04-03T09:00:12Z for policy=v3, targets=canary(2%)
Zoe: Canary live. running synthetic smoke now. initial smoke ok, token_ingress stable. :thumbsup:
Alex: Metrics: 429_rate=0.02% (baseline 0.01%), p95 latency +12ms, cache_hit_rate down 0.7% — within expected. Holding for 30m.
Carmen: Support queue: nothing customer-facing yet. monitoring replies from internal dev teams only.
Priya: Increment to 10% now. watch for correlation between client libraries that do parallel calls (we have a list in the rollout doc).
Alex: After bump: 429_rate=0.08%, p95 +40ms, cache_hit_rate -1.2% — still ok. No header_rejects.
Liam: Not seeing any infra anomalies. No SYN spikes.
Priya: Holding; will wait 2h before 50% per plan. If any of the rollback criteria hit, call it.
Carmen: Support ready for outreach; prepared a short note for affected customers.
Alex: 1h10m into canary — 429_rate creeping to 0.4% and concentrated on a handful of keys (api_key_hash a1b2...). Investigating request patterns.
Zoe: I see one high-volume client with many small parallel requests; they'd be impacted by the shorter burst window. Are they eligible for an override?
Priya: We can roll a temporary override for that key: rps=25, burst_window=2s, scoped to that api_key_hash. But that's manual — needs approval. Carmen, can we reach out to that customer proactively?
Carmen: Yes, we can. I'll draft outreach. If they confirm heavy parallelism, grant override and schedule a follow-up to recommend batching or client-side rate limiter.
Liam: Given concentration on single key and not broad regression, I'm leaning to continue to 50% and issue targeted override if they accept. Any objections?
Alex: I'd rather pause the ramp to 50% for 30m while we observe impact post-override. If override reduces 429s for that key and no new clusters appear, proceed.
Priya: Agree — pause ramp. Liam, hold rollback key but don't flip. Zoe, apply a temporary override and I'll document it.
Zoe: Applied override for api_key_hash=a1b2... with rps=25 and burst_window=2s (patch id: or-9876). Monitoring now.
Alex: After override: target key 429s dropped by 93% in 6m. Global 429_rate back to 0.09%. p95 stable.
Priya: Great. Proceeding with scheduled 50% bump in 40m. Documenting lessons: include default burst_window impacts, recommend adding per-client overrides in policy UI, and update the rollout checklist.
Carmen: I'll send the note to the affected customer explaining the temporary override and recommended client changes.
Liam: Good work. Postmortem items: longer-term we should consider a staged reduction in burst_window with feature flag to give clients notice.
Priya: Agreed. I'll create a follow-up action item ticket. Thanks everyone. :tada:
